correctness.rationale: For uniform q-ary input, adjacent inequality indicators are iid Bernoulli. Effective matchings are injective as outputs and yield Fibonacci products over maximal inequality runs. A first-zero decomposition supplies the exact real-moment recurrence and generating function; positivity and aperiodicity prove a unique dominant simple pole. Its analytic pressure gives, by differentiation, strict positive variance and a CLT, and by Gärtner–Ellis an LDP. The Binet/geometric calculation proves the large-q expansion and strict gap. The packaged program exhaustively checks 53260 words and rational moments, independently of the infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The 2017 primary paper provides the Fibonacci-product ball formula (Theorem 16) and arithmetic mean recurrence (Theorem 18), both explicitly credited. These do not themselves assert the log-volume pressure, its derivatives/CLT, the LDP, or the positive quantitative annealed–quenched gap. The July 21, 2026 primary paper addresses correction/detection/covering and capacity, not the uniform random-center distribution. Searches of indexed mathematical results for the exact formulations and alternate aliases found no equivalent statement; this remains qualified by risks of unindexed stochastic-reward presentations.
residual_risks: The deterministic center-wise factorization is already published. Its probabilistic consequences may have been derived elsewhere under the name random matching polynomial, renewal-reward pressure, or a similar alias.

The related June 25, 2026 local-criterion preprint was inspected only through a public abstract; its coding-construction topic makes matching distributional coverage unlikely, but it was not exhaustively read.
Generic renewal and analytic combinatorics limit theorems are background, and the proof claims novelty only for the explicit channel-specific assertions, not for those general tools.

value.rationale: Radius-one output-ball sizes vary exponentially with the center, and the earlier arithmetic mean conceals typical ambiguity. The fully specified log-volume pressure, central Gaussian fluctuations and large deviations quantify natural coding-geometric statistics across centers, not a hand-picked small case. A strictly positive annealed-versus-quenched exponent gap for each finite q, with an explicit large-q coefficient, gives a structural and practically interpretable distinction between typical and average neighborhood growth. No unsupported code-capacity gain is asserted.
